title: Muang Thai Chiang Mai Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2023 Race Was Like
seo_title: Chiang Mai Marathon Review: 3am Start, Weather, Finish Times
meta_description: Chiang Mai Marathon review from the 17 December 2023 race: 20°C and 88% humidity at 3am, 884 marathon finishers, a 4:44 median, and the cut-offs and shuttle now.
dek: What the Chiang Mai Marathon on 17 December 2023 was like, from its official results and the airport weather: how cool the night really was, how fast the field ran, and how the current format and cut-offs compare.
verdict: Enter if you want a cool-season marathon in northern Thailand with a 3am start and a field that runs quicker than most in the region. On 17 December 2023 the airport recorded 20°C at 3am, falling to 19°C before dawn, with almost no wind but 88% to 94% humidity, so it was mild rather than cold. The race had 884 marathon finishers and 937 in the half; half the marathon field finished inside 4:44, and a quarter broke four hours. The current format is point to point from Tha Phae Gate to Mae Rim, with a seven-hour marathon limit and a free shuttle back, but the 2023 route itself is not documented, and the results held here stop at 2023.

sections.heading: The Course: From the Old City Gate to Mae Rim
paragraphs: In its current form the marathon and half marathon start at Tha Phae Gate, on the east side of Chiang Mai's old city, and finish at the King Naresuan the Great Monument in Mae Rim district, north of the city. The 10 km and 3 km start and finish at Tha Phae Gate [1]. No route map for the 2023 race could be found, so it is not confirmed that the 2023 marathon used the same finish.

The organiser describes the route as flat with no hills [1]. One race database instead puts the marathon's elevation gain at about 280 m and calls the profile rolling [2]. Expect a mostly flat road course with some gentle climbing rather than a pancake.

sections.heading: The Weather: Mild and Damp, Not Cold
paragraphs: Chiang Mai airport, on the south-west edge of the city, recorded 20°C at 3am on race morning, with a dew point of 18°C, 88% humidity and a 1-knot wind [3]. It cooled to 19°C with 94% humidity from 5am to 6.30am, then warmed to 21°C at 8am, 24°C at 9am and 25°C at 10am [3].

That is warmer than the organiser's current guide, which expects 12°C to 18°C on race day [1]. It was still good running weather by Thai standards, but with the dew point close to the air temperature the air was saturated and still. A runner who did the 2024 race chose it partly because the 3am start is cooler than running during the day, and found the last 10 km the hardest part [4].
The time you finish decides the race you get: with a 3am start, a four-hour marathoner was done by about 7am at 20°C, while a six-hour runner finished at 9am, when it had reached 24°C [3].

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The organiser's current page does not list aid stations [1]. Its limits are seven hours for the marathon (10am), three and a half hours for the half (7.30am) and an hour and a half for the 10 km (6.30am) [1].

Measured against those limits, the 2023 field was comfortably inside them: 98.9% of marathon finishers were within seven hours and 98.9% of half marathoners within three and a half. Ten marathoners are listed beyond seven hours, the slowest in 7:14:34 [5]. The 2023 cut-offs themselves were not found.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The 2023 marathon had 884 finishers, down 7.5% from 956 in 2022 [5][6]. The top ten ran between 2:41:32 and 2:55:42; the fastest woman ran 3:03:07 and the tenth woman 3:24:15 [5].

This is a quicker field than most Southeast Asian marathons. The median finish was 4:44:06, six minutes faster than in 2022; 25.2% broke four hours and 62.4% broke five, and 90% were home inside 6:17:02 [5][6].

The half marathon had 937 finishers (922 in 2022). The top ten ran 1:09:15 to 1:21:05, the median was 2:18:05, almost identical to 2022, and 28.0% broke two hours [5][6]. Women made up 23% of marathon finishers, up from 19% in 2022, and 36% of the half [5][6].

Prize money now goes five deep: in the marathon, THB 7,000 to 3,000 for first to fifth in each age group, and THB 5,000 to 2,000 overall in the half [1]. With a tenth-place woman at 3:24:15 in 2023, a strong age-group runner has a realistic chance of a prize.

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: For 2026 the race expo and pack collection are at Tha Phae Gate on 18 and 19 December, 10am to 6pm; runners landing after 5pm on the Saturday are asked to email the organiser to arrange collection [1].

Because the marathon and half finish in Mae Rim, a free shuttle runs from the King Naresuan monument back to Tha Phae Gate from 6.30am to 10.30am on race day [1]. Marathon finishers get a finisher T-shirt as well as the race shirt and medal [1]. Entry fees are not refundable [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a December marathon in the best weather Thailand offers, and a field with enough depth that a sub-four-hour run puts you in the top quarter. The point-to-point course and free return shuttle make it straightforward, and the half marathon is a good option for a first race at that distance: in 2023, 98.9% of half marathoners finished inside today's 3:30 limit.

Think twice if you are counting on cold air: the 2023 race started at 20°C, not the 12°C to 18°C the organiser suggests, with the humidity near saturation. Pace for warm, damp air until the race-week forecast says otherwise.
The 2026 race is on Sunday 20 December [1].
This review draws on the organiser's current race information, a race database, airport weather records, one runner's account of the 2024 race, and the official results of the 2022 and 2023 races.

faqs.question: What time does the Chiang Mai Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Very early. Under the current schedule the marathon starts at 3am and the half marathon at 4am, both from Tha Phae Gate, with the 10 km at 5am and the 3 km Smile Run at 5.20am. The 2024 race also started at 3am, which runners use to avoid the daytime heat.

faqs.question: How cold is it at the Chiang Mai Marathon?
faqs.answer: Milder than many expect. At 3am on 17 December 2023 Chiang Mai airport recorded 20°C with a dew point of 18°C and 88% humidity, cooling only to 19°C before dawn and reaching 25°C by 10am. The organiser's guide suggests 12°C to 18°C, so check the forecast before choosing kit.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the Chiang Mai Marathon?
faqs.answer: Under the current rules, seven hours for the marathon (10am), three and a half hours for the half marathon (7.30am) and an hour and a half for the 10 km (6.30am). In 2023, 98.9% of marathon finishers and 98.9% of half marathon finishers were inside those limits.

faqs.question: How fast is the Chiang Mai Marathon field?
faqs.answer: Quicker than most in the region. In 2023 the median marathon finish was 4:44:06, a quarter of finishers broke four hours and the top ten ran 2:41:32 to 2:55:42. The median half marathon took 2:18:05, with 28% of finishers under two hours.

faqs.question: How do you get back from the finish in Mae Rim?
faqs.answer: On the free race-day shuttle. The marathon and half marathon finish at the King Naresuan the Great Monument in Mae Rim, and a shuttle runs from there back to the start at Tha Phae Gate from 6.30am to 10.30am. The 10 km and 3 km start and finish at Tha Phae Gate.

editorial_notes: Reinstated 2026-11-06: official results for the 17 December 2023 race are now on file (and for 18 December 2022), so the review is written about the 2023 race and attached to the 20 December 2026 edition. Later editions (2024 and 2025) were run, but no results for them are held and no detail about them is used beyond one 2024 runner's blog. Finish-time figures are Run SEA's own analysis of the SportStats results; no times were dropped as timing errors; one half-marathon time of 4:40:55 is an outlier. Only marathon and half-marathon results are held. Weather is from Chiang Mai airport METAR observations. Course, start times, cut-offs, shuttle and prizes are the organiser's current (2026) information; the 2023 route, finish and cut-offs were not found. Runners are not named. No rating.
